exposure: simulation-based training program in shoulder dystocia (pre-training, initial training, systematic training periods)
cohort: The study participants are mother-baby dyads who experienced shoulder dystocia at a tertiary center in Madrid, Spain, between 2015 and 2023.
finding: Simulation-based training significantly reduced the rate of permanent obstetric brachial plexus palsy without increasing the caesarean section rate or worsening other perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The study found no increase in the caesarean section rate following the implementation of the simulation training program.
